abstract: |
  Public biomedical data resources are central scientific
  infrastructure, but in our experience their evaluation is fragmented:
  each funded program tracks its own metrics, hindering portfolio-level
  comparison. We propose a framework of three questions about any data
  resource: is anyone better off (*public value*), can the data be
  trusted and reused (*data quality and reusability*), and can the
  resource keep running (*operations and finance*). We expect the
  relative priority of these domains to shift across a resource's
  lifecycle, so uniform metric panels risk undervaluing
  infrastructure-building. An NIH Common Fund dashboard collects some of
  these measures across 19 programs, without phase priorities. Funders
  and resource communities should agree on shared indicators and test
  the priorities together, grounding portfolio decisions in common
  evidence.
---
